title: From a VM object to a running guest
summary: Follow a VirtualMachine from kubectl to a guest running in a launcher pod.

steps.n: The user applies a VirtualMachine object and the API server validates it.
virt-controller watches the object and decides that an instance must run.
The controller creates a VirtualMachineInstance and a virt-launcher pod through the API.
The normal scheduler places the pod on a node and virt-handler on that node sees it.
virt-handler asks libvirt inside the launcher pod to start the QEMU domain.
The guest boots, the VMI reports an IP, and the user can open the console.

title: Installing KubeVirt on a cluster
summary: Two manifests turn a plain cluster into one that can run VMs.

steps.n: The admin applies the operator manifest, which creates the operator and the CRDs.
The admin creates the KubeVirt custom resource that says what to install.
The operator reads the resource and decides which components and versions to deploy.
It deploys virt-api, virt-controller and a virt-handler on every schedulable node.
virt-handler and the device plugin advertise the kvm device if /dev/kvm exists.
The resource reports Available and the admin can start a first VM.

title: Run strategies and the VM lifecycle
summary: See how Always, Manual and Halted change what happens to the instance.

steps.n: The user sets runStrategy to Always on the VirtualMachine.
virt-controller notices that no instance exists though one should run.
It creates the VirtualMachineInstance, which then moves through Scheduling to Running.
The guest powers off unexpectedly and the VMI ends.
Because the strategy is Always, the controller creates a new VMI automatically.
The user changes the strategy to Halted for maintenance.
The controller deletes the VMI and the VM object remains with its disks and settings.

title: Importing a golden image and cloning it
summary: A DataVolume imports an OS image once and clones it for new VMs.

steps.n: The user creates a DataVolume with an http source for the OS image.
CDI starts an importer pod that downloads and converts the image.
The importer writes the raw disk into a PVC that becomes the golden image.
A new VM asks for a DataVolume whose source is the golden PVC.
CDI clones the golden PVC, using a fast storage copy when the driver supports it.
The cloned PVC is bound and the VM can boot from its own copy.

title: Why a disk decides whether a VM can migrate
summary: Follow two VMs, one on RWO and one on RWX, through a migration request.

steps.n: The user asks KubeVirt to migrate two VMs.
KubeVirt checks the first VMI and finds a shared RWX block disk.
The target launcher can attach the same disk because storage allows two nodes.
KubeVirt checks the second VMI and finds a ReadWriteOnce disk.
A second node cannot attach a RWO volume while the first still has it.
LiveMigratable is False for the second VMI, with a message naming the storage.

title: One VM on the pod network and a VLAN
summary: Trace traffic through masquerade and a Multus bridge.

steps.n: A pod in the cluster calls the Service that selects the VM.
The Service sends traffic to the launcher pod IP on the pod network.
Masquerade translates the address and forwards the packet to the guest.
The guest sends traffic for the legacy system out of its second NIC.
The legacy server replies over the bridge with the guest's VLAN address.
The guest's answer to the pod network passes back through the NAT.

title: First boot of a repeatable VM
summary: Combine an image, an instance type and cloud-init into a ready VM.

steps.n: The pipeline builds a golden image, boots a test VM, and publishes it.
The VM spec references the instance type medium for CPU and memory.
The VM spec clones the tested image as its root disk.
A cloud-init volume carries the user, SSH key and package list.
On first boot cloud-init creates the user and installs the guest agent.
The guest agent connects and the pipeline marks the VM ready.

title: Failure and recovery: a migration that never finishes
summary: A busy VM dirties memory faster than it is copied, and a policy fixes it.

steps.n: The operator drains a node and evictionStrategy LiveMigrate creates a migration.
The controller starts a target launcher and attaches the shared disk.
The source launcher sends memory pages to the target over the network.
A busy database rewrites pages faster than the link can send them.
Pages are resent again and again, so the remaining difference never gets small.
The progress timeout fires and the migration fails while the drain waits.
The operator adds a policy with auto-converge and more bandwidth for database VMs.
Auto-converge slows the guest, the copy converges, and the switch happens within seconds.

title: What a VM pod must reserve
summary: Add up guest memory, overhead and dedicated CPU into pod resources.

steps.n: The scheduler starts from the guest memory the VM asks for.
KubeVirt adds memory for QEMU, libvirt and device emulation.
The sum becomes the pod request and the limit must be at least as large.
With the static CPU manager and Guaranteed QoS the pod gets exclusive cores.
If hugepages are requested the node must have them reserved or the pod waits.
When the node can satisfy everything, the launcher pod is scheduled.

title: A consistent snapshot and restore
summary: Freeze the guest, snapshot the disks, and restore to a new VM.

steps.n: The user creates a snapshot object that names the VM.
KubeVirt asks the guest agent to freeze file systems for a moment.
It asks the CSI driver for a VolumeSnapshot of each PVC.
Once snapshots are created the guest is thawed and writes resume.
Later the user creates a restore object that names the snapshot.
The VM is restored from the snapshot with its disks and definition.

title: Failure and recovery: old launchers after an upgrade
summary: The control plane upgrades but running VMs keep the old version.

steps.n: The admin applies a newer operator manifest.
virt-api, virt-controller and virt-handler are replaced with the new version.
Running VMs stay on their old virt-launcher until they restart or migrate.
The control plane is healthy, so no alert shows that VMs lag behind.
Weeks later the admin lists the launcher image version of each VMI and finds the old one.
The admin sets workloadUpdateMethods to LiveMigrate in the KubeVirt resource.
The controller migrates VMs in batches to launchers of the new version.
All VMs run the new version, and non-migratable ones are listed for a planned restart.

title: One migration wave from VMware
summary: Move a group of VMs with conversion, testing and cutover.

steps.n: The planner lists VMs, maps networks and storage, and creates a plan.
Forklift connects to vCenter and reads the VM disks and settings.
virt-v2v adapts each guest and the disks are copied into PVCs.
The converted VM boots in a test network and the application is checked.
The planner agrees a window with users and keeps the source VM powered off.
DNS or load balancer targets switch to the new VM.
